# 22 Visualising Geospatial Point Data

## 23 Overview

Proportional symbol maps (also known as graduate symbol maps) are a class of maps that use the visual variable of size to represent differences in the magnitude of a discrete, abruptly changing phenomenon, e.g. counts of people. Like choropleth maps, you can create classed or unclassed versions of these maps. The classed ones are known as range-graded or graduated symbols, and the unclassed are called proportional symbols, where the area of the symbols are proportional to the values of the attribute being mapped.

### 23.1 Learning Outcome

By the end of this hands-on exercise, you will acquire the following skills by using appropriate R packages:

- To import an aspatial data file into R.
- To convert it into simple point feature data frame and at the same time, to assign an appropriate projection reference to the newly create simple point feature data frame.
- To plot interactive proportional symbol maps.

## 24 Getting Started

Before we get started, we need to ensure that tmap package of R and other related R packages have been installed and loaded into R.

```{r}
pacman::p_load(sf, tmap, tidyverse)
```

## 25 Geospatial Data Wrangling

### 25.1 The Data

The data set use for this hands-on exercise is called SGPools_svy21. The data is in csv file format.

### 25.2 Data Import and Preparation

Import SGPools_svy21.csv into R:

```{r}
sgpools <- read_csv("data/SGPools_svy21.csv")
```

Examine if the data file has been imported correctly:

```{r}
list(sgpools)
```

### 25.3 Creating a sf Data Frame from an Aspatial Data Frame

Convert sgpools data frame into a simple feature data frame:

```{r}
sgpools_sf <- st_as_sf(sgpools, 
                       coords = c("XCOORD", "YCOORD"),
                       crs = 3414)
```

Display the basic information of the newly created sgpools_sf:

```{r}
list(sgpools_sf)
```

## 26 Drawing Proportional Symbol Map

Turn on the interactive mode of tmap:

```{r}
tmap_mode("view")
```

### 26.1 It All Started with an Interactive Point Symbol Map

Create an interactive point symbol map:

```{r}
tm_shape(sgpools_sf) + 
  tm_bubbles(fill = "red",
             size = 1,
             col = "black",
             lwd = 1)
```

### 26.2 Lets Make It Proportional

Draw a proportional symbol map by assigning Gp1Gp2 Winnings to size visual attribute:

```{r}
tm_shape(sgpools_sf) + 
  tm_bubbles(fill = "red",
             size = "Gp1Gp2 Winnings",
             col = "black",
             lwd = 1)
```

### 26.3 Lets Give It a Different Colour

Improve the proportional symbol map using colour visual attribute:

```{r}
tm_shape(sgpools_sf) + 
  tm_bubbles(fill = "OUTLET TYPE", 
             size = "Gp1Gp2 Winnings",
             col = "black",
             lwd = 1)
```

### 26.4 I Have a Twin Brothers :)

Create multiple maps with synchronised zoom and pan settings using tm_facets():

```{r}
tm_shape(sgpools_sf) + 
  tm_bubbles(fill = "OUTLET TYPE", 
             size = "Gp1Gp2 Winnings",
             col = "black",
             lwd = 1) + 
  tm_facets(by = "OUTLET TYPE",
            nrow = 1,
            sync = TRUE)
```

Switch tmap's Viewer back to plot mode:

```{r}
tmap_mode("plot")
```
